text.p: Typhoon Rosie, with 110 mph winds, is near 25.1n/133.3e, moving north northeast at 12 mph. Rosie will continue its track, weakening, and should have top winds of 75-80 mph when it makes landfall in southwestern Honshu, Japan, on Saturday. Rosie will likely produce storm surge coastal flooding, heavy rainfall leading to flooding and mudslides, and wind damage, with the worst likely occurring in southwestern and central Honshu during Saturday.

Moderate to heavy rain may develop later Friday into Saturday in northeastern Europe, including Poland, the Czech Republic, and eastern Germany, where recent flooding has been severe. Additional flooding is likely to occur with the next round of rain.

Showers and thunderstorms scattered across Bangladesh are leading to additional flooding problems in areas that have already seen severe flooding during the past couple of weeks. Additional property damage and crop loss may result.
